text.check.rules.ok: Who gets an issue in each status and who may move it follow the roles.
text.check.rules.differ: Assignees and gates do not follow the roles: {{count}} transitions.

text.fix.transitions.check: check {{total}} transitions and add the missing ones
text.fix.board.create: create a board with the template columns
text.fix.board.columns: add columns {{names}} and put them in flow order
text.fix.board.order: put the columns in flow order
text.fix.rules: set transition rules: assignees by role, gates for roles

text.template.design-dev.title: Design → development
text.template.design-dev.about: Design goes first: versions are made and reviewed, the main one is chosen. The approved design becomes a development issue and goes through implementation and testing. It is the same issue from the first request to the check of the result.
text.template.design-dev.status.Design: a design version is being made
text.template.design-dev.status.Design Review: a version is ready: people compare versions and write notes
text.template.design-dev.role.design: reviews versions, writes notes, chooses the main one
text.template.design-dev.role.lead: decides whether the design goes to development
text.template.design-dev.role.qa: checks the result and closes the issue
text.template.design-dev.type.Task: one issue per element: its design and its development
text.template.design-dev.type.Story: a larger piece of work in parts
text.template.design-dev.rule.done: Done only after Human Testing: AI Testing cannot close an issue.
text.error.no_login: No Jira login: enter it on the Connection step.
text.error.login: An email and an Atlassian API token are required.
text.error.site: A Jira address looks like name.atlassian.net.
text.error.project_key: A Jira project key is 2–10 Latin letters and digits, starting with a letter: «{{key}}».
text.error.role_empty: Role «{{role}}» must keep at least one person of the project.
text.error.no_project: No Jira project is chosen: the Project step.
text.error.no_space: This host keeps no space: no project, epic or sync.
text.error.epic_key: An epic key looks like {{project}}-12, not «{{raw}}».
text.error.epic_missing: {{key}} is not in Jira, or the login cannot see it.
text.error.epic_project: {{key}} is in project {{other}}, and the issues of this space go to {{project}}.
text.error.epic_type: {{key}} is not an epic but «{{type}}»: an item goes only under an epic.
text.error.no_item: There is no item «{{id}}» in this space.
text.page.title: Jira for the project
text.page.about: The project's items become Jira issues by themselves and move along the “{{template}}” flow — no need to go to Jira.
text.page.free.title: What the service writes to Jira
text.page.free.text: The template — with the “Apply the template” button on the Project step. The project's issues — when the sync is on, the Sync step.
text.page.step.connection.title: Connection
text.page.step.template.title: Template
text.page.step.project.title: Project
text.page.step.roles.title: Roles
text.page.step.sync.title: Sync
text.page.need_project: First choose or create a Jira project on the Project step.
text.page.conn.title: Jira login
text.page.conn.about: A Jira Cloud site, and the email and API token of the person the service works as: it reads the project, applies the template and keeps the issues. Another site or account — enter it here: each site has its own projects and roles.
text.page.conn.none: No Jira login: enter the address, the email and an API token below.
text.page.conn.works: **The login works.** Choose the Jira project for this project on the Project step.
text.page.conn.no_answer: Jira {{site}} did not answer — check the address and the token.
text.page.conn.checking: Checking the login: reading the project from Jira…
text.page.conn.read: **The login works.** Jira answered: project {{project}} is read as it is.
text.page.login.token_new: a new token replaces the old one
text.page.login.note: The token is kept on this computer, only for you, and goes only to Jira — never to the page, logs or colleagues. The service writes to Jira the template — with your “Apply the template” button — and the project's issues — once you switch the sync on.
text.page.tpl.transitions: Transitions — {{count}}; a row is where from, a column is where to
text.page.tpl.named: Transitions are named after the status they lead to.
text.page.tpl.roles: Roles — who leads an issue (a transition rule assigns it)
text.page.tpl.gate: only this role moves an issue into {{gates}}
text.page.proj.title: Which project follows the template
text.page.proj.about: The service checks the project against the template: the kind of project, statuses and their categories, transitions, the initial status, board columns, issue types. What differs goes in with one button.
text.page.proj.choose: Choose a Jira project above or create a new one from the template.
text.page.proj.nothing: Nothing to fix: everything that can be checked matches the template.
text.page.mk.title: A new project from the template
text.page.mk.about: an empty team-managed Jira project — and at once the statuses, transitions, rules and columns of the template
text.page.mk.no_right: only a Jira administrator can create a project — this login cannot
text.page.mk.name: Name
text.page.mk.bad_key: A key is 2–10 Latin letters and digits, starting with a letter: for example DS or MX2.
text.page.mk.taken: Project {{key}} is already in Jira — choose it above or type another key.
text.page.mk.busy: Creating {{key}} and applying the template — usually under a minute…
text.page.mk.go: Create the project and apply the template
text.page.mk.toast_ok: Project {{key}} is created, the template is in
text.page.apply.title: Apply the template — one request to Jira
text.page.apply.rules: transition rules: assignees by role and who may move an issue — {{transitions}}
text.page.apply.same: statuses and transitions already follow the template — not touched
text.page.apply.dry_busy: Jira checks the template — nothing is written…
text.page.apply.done: **The template is in {{key}}.** Statuses, transitions and columns follow the template; the check above is of the new Jira.
text.page.apply.dry_ok: **Jira checked the template — no errors.** Nothing has changed in the project yet.
text.page.apply.confirm: **Apply the template to {{key}}?** Statuses, transitions and rules of the project become as in the template — for every issue type but the epic; no issue moves. Only a person in Jira can bring back what was there before.
text.page.cols.add: In {{key}}: board → “⋯” → Configure board → Columns — add {{names}} and put the columns in flow order: {{order}}.
text.page.cols.order: In {{key}}: board → “⋯” → Configure board → Columns — put the columns in flow order: {{order}}.
text.page.cols.why_manual: These statuses existed already; Jira adds a column for a status only together with a new status.
text.page.cols.why_error: Jira did not let the columns change: {{error}}.
text.page.cols.why_order: The columns did not get into flow order.
text.page.cols.added: Columns {{names}} are added to the board.
text.page.plan.title: Plan — {{steps}}
text.page.plan.only: Only a team-managed Jira Software project takes the template; new statuses, categories and columns need an empty project.
text.page.roles.title: Who leads an issue
text.page.roles.reading: Reading the people of the project from Jira…
text.page.roles.about: A role has one person or several. An issue entering a status is assigned to the one chosen in “assign to” — Jira assigns only one; “nobody” — the issue stays unassigned and anyone of the role takes it. Only the people of the role and the login the service works as can move an issue into a gate ({{gates}}). These are transition rules in Jira — they work when an issue is moved by hand too.
text.page.roles.single: **{{key}} has one person — {{name}}.** Every role is on them. When other people come, assign them here, and the rules go in with the same button.
text.page.roles.single_admin: **{{key}} has one person — {{name}} (Jira admin).** Every role is on them. When other people come, assign them here, and the rules go in with the same button.
text.page.roles.nobody: nobody — anyone of the role takes it
text.page.roles.gate: only the people of the role and the service login move an issue into {{gates}}
text.page.roles.saved: The roles are saved on this computer.
text.page.roles.differ: Transition rules in {{key}} do not follow these roles yet — the button sends them to Jira.
text.page.roles.follow: Transition rules in {{key}} follow these roles.
text.page.roles.refused: Jira did not take the template: {{errors}}
text.page.sync.title: The project's issues — to {{key}}
text.page.sync.about: From the moment it is on, every new item of the project becomes an issue in {{key}} by itself and moves along the statuses after the host. The service's login writes — {{site}}; another site or account has its own project and sync.
text.page.sync.pick: Items that exist already — add them now? Unticked ones are not written until you press “Add” next to them
text.page.sync.not_ready: First bring {{key}} in line with the template — the Project and Roles steps.
text.page.sync.on_add: Switch the sync on and add {{issues}}
text.page.sync.on_sub: {{site}} · since {{since}} — new items become issues by themselves
text.page.sync.on_sub_epic: {{site}} · since {{since}} — new items become issues by themselves · under epic {{epic}}
text.page.sync.empty: No items in this project yet — the first one becomes an issue by itself.
text.page.sync.how: An issue follows its item: the service moves it to the status the host gives the item, along the transitions of the template; new notes of the item become comments. One item — one issue.
text.page.key.failed: Jira did not take the last change: {{error}}
text.page.key.add_tip: The item was there before the sync was switched on — add its issue now
text.page.epic.title: Epic for the issues
text.page.epic.about: The issue of every item goes under this epic of {{key}} (the Parent field in Jira). Epics, for example by screens, are made in Jira by hand; here goes the epic's key: the service checks that it is in {{key}} and that it is an epic.
text.page.epic.what_on: Issues already in Jira go under the new epic right after saving.
text.page.epic.what_off: Once the sync is on, the issue of every item is created under it at once.
text.page.epic.ok: Issues of the items go under epic {{link}} “{{summary}}”.
text.page.epic.ok_status: Issues of the items go under epic {{link}} “{{summary}}” · {{status}}.
text.page.epic.bad: Jira does not give epic **{{key}}**: {{problem}}. Issues are created and move along the statuses without an epic, each with an error, until the key is fixed or the epic removed.
text.page.epic.toast_set: Issues of the items go under epic {{epic}}
text.page.epic.toast_clear: The epic is removed: new issues are created without it
text.page.n.drop: {{count}} extra to remove|{{count}} extra to remove
